pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Changing the fixture behavior to keep kind and API version intact during `List` with `UnstructuredList` object.

/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

It makes possible to write unit-test with a regular `UnstructuredList`.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #80722

**Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.**:

Repository to reproduce the [issue](https://github.com/otaviof/unstructured-list-issue).

issue_context.title: Fixture List using Unstructured
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:

Using `k8s.io/client-go/testing/fixture.go`'s `List` method with `UnstructuredList` object, returns error duing `Decode` object. Along the path it has lost metadata kind and APIVersion.

**What you expected to happen**:

Metadata kind and APIVersion would be kept regardless.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Please consider the [example repo](https://github.com/otaviof/unstructured-list-issue) for more details. In short, the following snippet represents the issue:

``` go
func TestUnstructuredListIssue(t *testing.T) {
	d := getDeployment()
	s := scheme.Scheme

	require.Nil(t, appsv1.AddToScheme(s))

	objs := []runtime.Object{&d}
	fakeClient := fake.NewFakeClientWithScheme(s, objs...)

	uList := ustrv1.UnstructuredList{}
	uList.SetGroupVersionKind(schema.GroupVersionKind{
		Group:   "apps",
		Version: "v1",
		Kind:    "DeploymentList",
	})

	opts := client.ListOptions{
		Namespace:     ns,
		LabelSelector: labels.SelectorFromSet(matchLabels),
	}

	ctx := context.TODO()
	err := fakeClient.List(ctx, &opts, &uList)
	require.Nil(t, err)
}
```

And returns the following error:

```
&errors.errorString{s:"unmarshalerDecoder: Object 'Kind' is missing in '{\"metadata\":{},\"items\":[{\"metadata\":{\"name\":\"deployment\",\"namespace\":\"namespace\",\"creationTimestamp\":null,\"labels\":{\"app\":\"test\"}},\"spec\":{\"replicas\":1,\"selector\":{\"matchLabels\":{\"app\":\"test\"}},\"template\":{\"metadata\":{\"name\":\"deployment\",\"namespace\":\"namespace\",\"creationTimestamp\":null,\"labels\":{\"app\":\"test\"}},\"spec\":{\"containers\":[{\"name\":\"busybox\",\"image\":\"busybox:latest\",\"command\":[\"sleep\",\"3600\"],\"resources\":{}}]}},\"strategy\":{}},\"status\":{}}]}', error found in #10 byte of ...|tus\":{}}]}|..., bigger context ...|],\"resources\":{}}]}},\"strategy\":{}},\"status\":{}}]}|..."}
```

**Environment**:

This snippet is used in combination with Operator-SDK, and only runs during `go test`. The `client-go` version is: `20190228174230-b40b2a5939e4`.

/sig testing

it is expected, but is not desired. see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/80609

rather than working around this in lots of individual places, something like https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/80618/commits/faf14c724f0573ab47568e1a6f2c9a5455cf0305 would be a more systemic fix. I don't think we should complicate this code to work around this issue in one specific place
